clue.text: Cards that are, thank you very much, rubbish

parts.note: TA is informal British shorthand for thanks
rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a pack of cards as junk with a sarcastic thank-you.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarot pack is a set of cards used for fortune-telling.

clue.text: Lawsuit about empty theatrical building

indicators.note: about means the lawsuit's word goes around the other piece

parts.note: a lawsuit is a legal case

indicators.note: empty means the word theatrical is emptied of its inside letters, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Litigation over a theatre that has fallen vacant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' keeps only the outer letters of theatrical, and 'about' wraps the lawsuit around them.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle is a large fortified building, so the general word covers it as an example.

clue.text: A day to correspond will be enough

parts.note: to equate is to match or correspond

explanation.surface: A single day of letter-writing will suffice.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adequate is sufficient, just meeting the need.

clue.text: Strange rule in support of a government department

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece in support of another sits beneath it

parts.note: FO is the ... Office, a UK government department
to reign is to rule as a monarch

explanation.surface: An odd regulation backing a Whitehall ministry.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'in support of' places REIGN under FO.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreign can mean alien or unfamiliar, as in a foreign idea.

clue.text: Engineers the people into a form of government

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
the public means people in general

explanation.surface: Technicians are drafted into a political system for the masses.
explanation.definitionFit: A republic is a state governed by elected representatives with no monarch.

clue.text: One signs a release for timber treatment

indicators.note: release suggests letting the letters go free to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A person puts their name to a document freeing some wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood is seasoned by drying it out slowly before use, a standard woodworking process.

clue.text: How jaguar fought with rover?

parts.note: jaguar and rover look like car makes, but read them as a big feline and a roaming hound brawling, the idiom for fighting bitterly

explanation.surface: Two British car marques are imagined squaring up to each other.
explanation.walkthrough: Jaguar and Rover are both British car makes, which is the surface; the cryptic reading takes them as a feline and a canine.
explanation.definitionFit: To fight like this phrase is to quarrel fiercely, as the two animals are said to do.

clue.text: What is held as true could also be the reverse

indicators.note: says the word reads the same when turned back to front, so the reverse gives the same letters

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A principle might just as well be its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a belief or doctrine a person holds firmly.

clue.text: Part of the planet that is rising, swamped by motorists

indicators.note: swamped by means surrounded on both sides by the motoring letters

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation

indicators.note: rising in a down answer means the word is reads upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: A region of the world that is climbing is flooded with drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' is a link word; 'rising' reads is upwards in this down answer, and 'swamped by' sets it between the two letters of the motoring organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is a continent, one division of the Earth's land.

clue.text: Shop soiled bouquet one accepted

indicators.note: accepted means the piece for one is taken inside the jumbled letters
soiled suggests the flower arrangement is messed up, so its letters are muddled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A grubby bunch of flowers is taken in by a shopkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soiled' muddles the flowers into BOUTQUE, and 'accepted' takes the numeral one into that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A boutique is a small fashionable shop.

clue.text: Drink rackets

definitions.meaning: a fruit cordial diluted with water
the racket sport played in a walled court

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a soft cordial drink and the indoor sport also known as squash rackets.

clue.text: Midwives have a lot of time for this girl

indicators.note: Mid points to the middle letter of the word wives

parts.note: an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Birth attendants spend much time on one young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midwives' splits as Mid + wives: the middle letter of WIVES is V.
explanation.definitionFit: Vera is a girl's name.

clue.text: Good! Fish, fish and fish

parts.note: a ray is a flat cartilaginous fish
a ling is a long fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic seafood order: fish, then more fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The grayling is a freshwater fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Half fare, initially for Sunday match officials

indicators.note: half takes the second half of the word fare
initially takes the first letter of the word for

explanation.surface: A half-price ticket for a Sunday fixture's umpires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' gives RE, the back half of fare; 'initially' gives F from for.
explanation.definitionFit: Refs is the short form of referees, the officials who run a game.

clue.text: Eire put to flight and in a spin

indicators.note: put to flight means routed and scattered, so the letters are sent in disorder

explanation.surface: Ireland is routed and left reeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put to flight' reads as the anagram signal, but 'put' and 'to' are themselves fodder with Eire; 'flight' alone signals the scattering.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirouette is a ballet turn on one foot, a spin.

clue.text: Pitch black?

definitions.meaning: the quality of a musical sound
a shade or colour, as one of the hues on a chart

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a musical note's quality and a shade of colour, black being one example.

clue.text: Leftovers in short supply!

indicators.note: in signals that the letters are found inside the words short supply

explanation.surface: Scraps of food are scarce.
explanation.definitionFit: Orts are scraps of food left after a meal, an old word much loved by setters.

clue.text: One might follow his advice, of course, and lose

definitions.text: One might follow his advice, of course, and lose

parts.words: One might follow his advice, of course, and lose
parts.note: of course means at the racecourse: this is someone who recommends horses to back, whose punters may lose their stake

explanation.surface: A rueful comment that heeding someone's guidance naturally leads to failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' looks like 'naturally' but means on the racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipster sells predictions on races, and backers who follow them often lose money.

clue.text: Sailor putting the food in — to burn!

indicators.note: putting in means the food piece is placed inside the burning word

parts.note: to sear is to scorch or burn
fare is food provided at a meal

explanation.surface: A ship's cook puts the meal in and lets it char.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash and 'putting ... in' make the food go inside the verb meaning to scorch.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafarer is someone who travels by sea, a sailor.

clue.text: Sport dealing with hot goods

definitions.meaning: the sport of fighting with swords
receiving and selling stolen property; hot is slang for stolen

explanation.definitionFit: The word names swordplay as a sport and also trading in stolen goods, a fence being a dealer in loot.

clue.text: Very light ale brewed over in that place

indicators.note: over means the jumbled letters spread across and around the other piece
brewed suggests the beer's letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: there means in that place

explanation.surface: A pale beer has been brewed in a particular spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' turns the beer into EAL, and 'over' wraps those letters around the phrase for in that place.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means delicate and airy, so light it seems not of this world.

clue.text: International examination?

definitions.meaning: a full international cricket match between two countries

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a Test match, international cricket's top form, and an exam.

clue.text: To share is possible, if in range

indicators.note: is possible suggests the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Sharing could happen, provided you are close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if in range' sounds like 'within earshot'; the definition is just 'range'.
explanation.definitionFit: Earshot is the distance within which a sound can be heard, a range of hearing.

clue.text: Doctor with broken nails a picture!

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

indicators.note: broken suggests the letters of nails a are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A medic treats a patient with damaged fingernails, then exclaims at a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges NAILSA to NALISA after MO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mona Lisa is Leonardo da Vinci's famous portrait painting.

clue.text: Team's leader travels south for a day in Rome

indicators.note: in a down answer the first letter moving south means it drops to the bottom

parts.note: a side is a team

explanation.surface: A captain heads south to spend a day in the Italian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The S at the top of SIDE moves to the foot, giving IDES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ides was a fixed day in the Roman calendar, around the middle of each month.

clue.text: Possesses heroin and marijuana

parts.note: has means possesses
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Someone is caught carrying two kinds of drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hash is short for hashish, cannabis resin, the same drug family as marijuana.

clue.text: Calm corner of England before engagement

indicators.note: before means the first piece comes ahead of the second

parts.note: SE is the south-east, a corner of England
a date is an appointment or engagement

explanation.surface: Composure in the South East ahead of a planned meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate means quiet and composed, unhurried.

clue.text: The darling finally changed sides in fury

indicators.note: the final letter, right, switches to the other side, left

parts.note: anger means fury

explanation.surface: A beloved person suddenly turned against someone in a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: R and L are the usual abbreviations for right and left: ANGER's last letter R becomes L.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel is a term of endearment, like darling.

clue.text: Iron man showing characteristics of the opposite sex

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a man is a male

explanation.surface: A strongman displays traits usually thought womanly.
explanation.walkthrough: Seen from 'man', the opposite sex is women.
explanation.definitionFit: From a man's viewpoint, the other gender is women, so a woman is the opposite of male.

clue.text: Harsh pace, and not disheartened

parts.note: a stride is a step or pace

indicators.note: disheartened means the word not loses its heart, its middle letter

explanation.surface: A grim walk, yet nobody lost spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' strips O from not, leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Strident means loud and grating, harsh to the ear.

clue.text: Manoeuvre always on the road

indicators.note: on means the always piece is placed after the road piece

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a road
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: Constantly out driving.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer is to guide a vehicle's direction, to manoeuvre it.

clue.text: Payments owing links to the crown?

parts.note: royal means belonging to the crown
ties are links or connections

explanation.surface: Money due as a result of connections to the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'links to the crown' as royal ties.
explanation.definitionFit: Royalties are sums paid to an author or patent holder for each sale.
